key_findings.finding_1_policy_always_optional: Routes use ctx.policy ? hasInternalAccess(ctx.policy) : false (defensive pattern) - policy is optional in CanonicalAuthContext
key_findings.finding_2_service_receives_boolean: Services receive hasInternalAccess as boolean parameter, not full policy context
key_findings.finding_3_capability_checks_service_leve: Capability checks happen via ctx.verifiedCapabilities (set at wrapper), policy is not used by services for capability enforcement
key_findings.finding_4_policy_used_for_visibility: Policy is primarily used for internal access checks → visibility filtering, not capability-based access
key_findings.finding_5_role_separate_from_policy: Custom role resolution (resolveServerRole) is separate from PolicyContext, not integrated
key_findings.finding_6_workspace_membership_in_servic: Workspace membership validation happens in services, requires policy.userId or separate workspace context
key_findings.finding_7_defensive_pattern_acceptable: Defensive ctx.policy ? ... : false pattern is safe - no enforcement depends on policy being present

design_implications.implication_1: Policy can remain optional in CanonicalAuthContext - routes have defensive fallbacks
design_implications.implication_2: Services should NOT receive full PolicyContext - only specific booleans (hasInternalAccess) or computed values
design_implications.implication_3: Capability enforcement must NOT depend on policy - it uses ctx.verifiedCapabilities from wrapper
design_implications.implication_4: Internal access enforcement is secondary to capability enforcement, used for visibility filtering only
design_implications.implication_5: Workspace membership validation is service-level responsibility, not route-level capability check
design_implications.implication_6: Role-based auth (for admin ops) is separate concern from policy-based auth
